population: reply letter on the reanalysis of Killingsworth 2021's data: employed US adults

findings.text: Except at the 15th percentile, happiness rises significantly with income at every level of happiness studied

support.sentence: 1) With one exception, happiness rises significantly with Log(income) in all the quantile regressions shown in Fig. 1 .

findings.text: Only the 15th percentile of happiness rises below $100,000 and barely changes above it

support.sentence: 2) The exception is the 15th percentile, which rises relatively steeply below $100K but barely changes above $100K, consistent with the flattening pattern.
support.readBy: dossier agent (money-happiness), PMC11572976 full text, point 2

findings.text: The authors place Kahneman & Deaton's threshold at $100,000 after inflation, not $75,000 (the midpoint of a $60-90K band)

support.sentence: Adjusting for inflation, the predicted threshold beyond which a flattened pattern should be detectable in Killingsworth’s data was $100K.
